# Compose pack handoff

Pairing recipe when one assistant **drafts** a social post and another **posts** it. Not a site publish skill.

No account names. Caller supplies the destination and the pack rules.

## Writer (Chrome-free)

1. Output an exact paste pack only: **BODY** text.
2. No hashtags or images unless the caller pack includes them.
3. If pack MEDIA is none, do not put a URL or bare domain in BODY (the feed will auto-unfurl it into a card). Write the site name in words unless the pack explicitly allows unfurl.
4. One-tab / close leftover tabs including blanks are **notes** for the poster, not a browser job.
5. Do not open listing Chrome or the poster's compose Chrome. Do not open a second compose tab to help.

## Poster

1. Already one tab that is not another job's page. If leftovers exist: **STOP**.
2. Same-tab navigate only to the destination feed/compose URL the caller named. **Never type into the address bar.**
3. If pack MEDIA is none and BODY contains a URL or bare domain, **do not Post**. Return the pack to the writer.
4. Confirm the compose field is focused. Paste the pack **BODY** verbatim once.
5. **Read the composer against the pack before Post.** If garbled, truncated, or not a match: do not Post. Clear, paste once more, read again.
6. If the human said read before Post: **wait**. Do not Post until that read-back is done.
7. **Post** is a click on Post after read-back matches. Do **not** scroll-drag in the composer (a drag can submit).
8. Record the live URL. **Stop** every composer/poster session.
9. After live: do not open Chrome to strip an auto-unfurl card. Do not open a second composer.

## Hard stops

- If a live post URL already exists for this pack BODY, **do not Post again**.
- Never type into the address bar. Google Search of the destination URL means STOP, not a recovery path.
- Garbled or truncated paste means do not Post. Read-back first.
- Scroll-drag in the composer means do not. Drag can submit.
- One poster runner. Do not both drive the same desktop.
- Writer never helps by opening extra tabs.
- A full publish-path skill for that site still waits until a real live post URL exists (then still Post that BODY only once).

# LinkedIn feed paste pack

Chrome-free **writer** pack for a LinkedIn feed/share post. Do not publish from this skill. Poster uses linkedin-text-post. Pairing: compose-pack-handoff.

Caller supplies the exact BODY (already approved). Specific post text stays in a file/pack, not in this recipe. Do not invent copy, hashtags, or images. No account names.

1. Output a Chrome-free copy pack: **BODY** (exact). One-tab / close leftover tabs including blanks are **notes for the poster**, not a browser job for the writer.
2. Default: no hashtags, no images, no extra lines before or after BODY, unless the caller put them in the pack.
3. **If MEDIA is none:** do not put a URL or bare domain in BODY (the feed will auto-unfurl it into a card and the og:title becomes that site). Write the site name in words. If an unfurl card is wanted, the pack must say so explicitly.
4. LinkedIn share composer has no title field. Do not invent a headline.
5. Do not open LinkedIn or listing Chrome (Marketplace / Trade Me / eBay). Do not drive the poster's desktop.
6. Do not edit About, headline, or other profile fields from this skill.
7. If login/2FA is needed for posting, the **poster** stops and hands the computer to the human. Do not type credentials.
8. After a live post URL exists, keep the pack as the template for the next post. Do not post that same BODY again unless the caller asks to recycle it.

Do not bake in a specific person, employer, product, or post text.

# Listing copy pack

Use this when preparing the next Marketplace, Trade Me, or eBay listing of an already-priced part so fields are pasted, not rediscovered.

Caller supplies title, price, category, condition, location (city + country), freight policy, photos, and any footer. Do not invent copy, price, location, plate, or VIN.

1. Build a single labelled copy pack **before** opening the browser: TITLE, PRICE, LOCATION, CATEGORY, CONDITION, FREIGHT_LINE, DESCRIPTION (body + freight + footer), plus operator notes for that site.
2. Paste those blocks into the form. Do not retype fields from memory on listing 2+.
3. Location is whatever the caller stated (city + country). Confirm it on the form before Next/Publish. Do not trust a leftover location.
4. Freight line is whatever the caller stated (included under a weight cap, pickup, or buyer-pays). Do not invent postage.
5. **Trade Me shipping/pickup must match the description.** If the form forbids pick-ups, do not put a pickup line in the pack or on the form. Do not publish a pickup line when pick-ups are forbidden.
6. Optional pull-to-order / example-photo language and extra-parts footer only if the caller asked. Never add plate or VIN unless the caller supplied VIN for public use.
7. Trade Me vehicle parts: open Motors / car parts create first. Never general Marketplace create.
8. Facebook: use the Facebook Marketplace item listing skill. One tab. Photo required before Next. Skip Boost. Confirm location on the form.
9. After first successful publish on a site, reuse this pack and that site's shortest path for the next part. Do not re-walk menus.
10. Do not publish until a human has approved that listing's price and copy. Do not message buyers. Do not drive the listing browser if another assistant already has exclusive listing sessions — generate the pack only.

If a local generator or markdown pack already exists for this part type, run/open that instead of rewriting the blocks.

# Unique listing photos

Use this when two listings would otherwise share the same photo (Marketplace duplicate banner, same SKU family, or only one example shot exists).

1. Never reuse another live listing's photo on a different SKU.
2. If a second real photo of that SKU exists, use it.
3. If only one example image exists, make a distinct file: horizontal flip is enough. Keep the original for the first SKU. Do not overwrite the original.
4. Save the new file next to the listing photos with a SKU-specific name.
5. A Marketplace might-be-a-duplicate banner means the listing is not live. Fix the photo, then republish. Do not report that URL as listed.
6. Do not generate a fake product photo when a real or approved example already exists.

skills.name: Facebook Marketplace item listing
skills.description: Use this when publishing a Facebook Marketplace item from an approved pack: paste full DESCRIPTION, last line must include the pack footer before Publish or edit-save, unique photo, skip Boost. Missing footer = do not Publish.
skills.content:
---
name: Facebook Marketplace item listing
description: >-
  Use this when publishing a Facebook Marketplace item from an approved pack:
  paste full DESCRIPTION, last line must include the pack footer before Publish
  or edit-save, unique photo, skip Boost. Missing footer = do not Publish.
---
# Facebook Marketplace item listing

Publish one Marketplace **item** from an approved pack. Caller supplies copy, category, location, and the unique photo. Do not bake in a vehicle, city, account, listing URL, or a batch cap.

## Inputs

- Approved pack, verbatim: title, price, location (city + country), **full** description including freight lines and footer
- Category as the pack/form requires (vehicle parts: **Car parts**)
- Unique photo for this SKU (not another listing's photo)
- Human yes to publish

Stop if any of those are missing. Do not invent, paraphrase, or truncate copy.

## Path

1. Have the approved pack and a unique photo for this SKU.
2. Open `https://www.facebook.com/marketplace/create/item` in **one** tab on the existing session. Close leftover tabs and chat popups first.
3. **Title and price — clear, then paste. Never append.** Click the field (not the address bar). Select-all, delete, paste pack title / type only pack price digits. Read back: extra digits or leftover words = not the pack. If wrong, clear-paste **once** more, then **stop**. Do not start another runner.
4. Set location from the pack. Set category as the pack/form requires (vehicle parts: Car parts).
5. Paste the **full DESCRIPTION** (not a truncated body). Read back the **last line**: it must include the pack footer. If the footer or freight lines are missing, **do not Publish**. Same check before **edit-save**.
6. Add the unique photo. **Next**.
7. Before Publish (or edit-save): last line of DESCRIPTION still includes the pack footer. Confirm location + copy match the pack. **Publish**. **Skip Boost**.
8. Close the tab. Record the public item URL. Stop.

Listing 2+ of this type: same URL, same fields, paste the next pack. Do not rediscover, recategorise, or click-hunt.

If the create form reloads or wipes: refill from the pack **at most twice**. After two wipes, **stop**.

## Hard stops

- **One listing runner per SKU.** If one is running, do not start another. Stop means stop: no second fill on the same form.
- One tab only. No DevTools, no debugger, no address-bar typing. No CDP, Playwright, xdotool, shell-driven Chrome, or injecting clipboard into the browser from the shell.
- Extra digits or leftover words in title/price = **stop**, not another runner. Do not Publish.
- Missing pack footer (last line of DESCRIPTION) or freight lines = **do not Publish** and **do not edit-save**.
- After two form wipes, stop. Do not loop. Do not open DevTools to inspect why.
- Duplicate-listing banner = **not live**. Unique photo then retry, or abandon.
- A draft is not live. Do not message buyers. Do not Boost or spend.

# One tab stop

Use this before opening a website, and again if a tab appears on its own.

1. One job, one tab. If a tab is already open on the page you need, stay there. Do not open a second tab or a second window.
2. Leftover tabs at the start, a blank tab, or a second window: stop. Do not click tab close. Do not open a new tab to recover. Do not start another runner.
3. Do not type into the address bar. Do not use New Tab, Chrome plus, or a new window.
4. If sign-in is already done, do the job in that same tab. If sign-in is waiting on the human, stop on that screen. Do not open another site in a new tab.
5. After you stop, report one line: leftover tabs, waiting. Then idle until a new named job names one exact URL.

  for runners=0 before the next batch, HARD PARK means no wakes
---
# Named-job assignment

Use when handing work to a specialist.

## Rules
1. Named job only. Objective, inputs, definition of done, kill rules, what not to do.
2. One live runner per stream. Do not start a second Task, walker, or batch until the first reports runners=0 (actually stopped, not a stale idle ping).
3. Batch long jobs. Stop at the batch end and wait for the dispatcher before the next batch.
4. HARD PARK means idle: no dumps, no Chrome, no connector calls, no checkpoints, no pings until a new named job.
5. Event-driven waste watch only. Do not poll specialists on a timer while a long job is in flight.
6. If a tool error names the correct server or path, use that immediately. Do not retry the failed short name.
7. Do not overwrite another specialist's instructions unless the user approved that change (or granted standing authority that is still in force).

## After the job
Record what worked, what wasted usage, and what the user had to correct. Propose instruction changes; do not apply them until approved, unless standing authority exists.

skills.description: Use when proving a Cursor/Agent Plugin loads locally — schema validate, install under ~/.cursor/plugins/local, and record what loaded.
skills.content:
---
name: prove-plugin-local
description: >-
  Use when proving a Cursor/Agent Plugin loads locally — schema validate,
  install under ~/.cursor/plugins/local, and record what loaded.
---
# Prove a plugin locally

## Preconditions

Plugin directory has either:
- Agent Plugin: root `plugin.json` with agent-plugins `$schema`, or
- Cursor Plugin: `.cursor-plugin/plugin.json`

## Steps

1. **Schema.** Validate Agent `plugin.json` / `mcp.json` against https://agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.0.0/plugin.schema.json and `mcp.schema.json` (jsonschema or equivalent). Cursor manifests only need a kebab-case `name` (no agent `$schema`).
2. **MCP smoke.** If there is a stdio server: `node --check` (or language equivalent), then a live `initialize` + `tools/list` + one real `tools/call` against the public API when safe.
3. **Install path.** Copy into a **real directory** under `~/.cursor/plugins/local/<plugin-name>` (not a symlink whose target is outside that folder; Cursor rejects those).
4. **Loader.** Prefer running `@anysphere/cursor-plugins` `loadUserLocalPlugins({ userHomeDir })` when that package is available. Expect the plugin name, skills, rules, and mcp server ids.
5. **IDE.** Reload Window / Customize confirms components when running inside Cursor. Note org gate: Teams/Enterprise may require Allow Local Plugin Imports.
6. **Verify note.** Short file or chat note: paths, PASS/FAIL, what loaded vs what this environment cannot prove (Customize UI, org policy).

## Done when

Manifests valid, local install present as a real directory, and either the shared loader reports the plugin or you documented why the loader/IDE step was skipped.
